name: 4340 South Monaco (Lofts on Monaco)
award: 2024 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Shea Properties converted a vacant 124,000 sq ft, four-story 2001 office building at 4340 S. Monaco Street near the Denver Tech Center into 143 income-restricted apartments for households at 30% to 70% AMI, financed with 2024 Round Two federal 4% and accelerated state credits and $26.6M of City and County of Denver bonds; it opened as Lofts on Monaco in June 2026.
why_it_matters: It is the Denver region's first post-pandemic office-to-affordable conversion to reach completion, and the application shows the pieces that made it work: a preserved DDA basis boost, a seller carryback note, a Denver Housing Authority tax-exemption partnership and bond cap pooled from Denver, Centennial and Englewood.

status.label: Completed and leasing (opened June 2026)
status.detail: BusinessDen reported that Lofts on Monaco opened in mid-June 2026, and the general contractor JHL Constructors announced the grand opening on 2026-07-27 with residents moving in. Shea closed on the building purchase in April 2025 and did the conversion over about a year.

next_step: Watch for CHFA's placed-in-service record (8609s) and stabilized occupancy, and for the permanent loan conversion of the Denver bonds.

key_numbers.meaning: 23 studios, 89 one-bedroom, 25 two-bedroom, 3 three-bedroom and 3 four-bedroom units, at 30%, 60% and 70% AMI with income averaging.
About $23.5M over 10 years, plus $1,800,000 of accelerated state credit; the application priced total credit equity at $28.07M ($19.97M federal, $8.1M state).

key_numbers.value: $26,600,000 in City and County of Denver bonds
key_numbers.meaning: Denver is the issuer (council authorized up to $29M, Series 2025A and 2025B); the application says the cap came from Denver ($17.7M), Centennial ($6.7M) and Englewood ($2.1M).
Per the application, including a $12M building purchase (BusinessDen) partly financed by a $9.84M seller carryback note.

facts.value: 4340 S. Monaco Street, Denver 80237 (Southmoor Park statistical neighborhood, next to the Denver Tech Center, across the street from Cherry Hills Village)
N, F: new, family in the award report; the applicant report and the CHFA letter of intent list it as acquisition/rehab
Four-story, about 124,000 sq ft precast concrete office building built in 2001, formerly occupied by Invesco, vacant about six years; about 176 surface spaces plus access to about 285 garage spaces

Interior demolition and rebuild: new mechanical, plumbing, electrical and fire sprinkler systems, elevator upgrades, roof resealed; existing windows and exterior kept. Change of use to Type IIB construction
Rezoned from B-4 with waivers and conditions (UO-1, UO-2) to PUD-G 34 for the 12.58-acre 4340-4350 S. Monaco parcel (case 2024I-00027, Council Bill 24-0617), passed 2024-08-12
Denver Housing Authority named as special limited partner, per the application
All-electric design, Enterprise Green Communities and Energy Star; resident services with a local YMCA (after-school, nutrition, wellness, financial planning)
Less than 1 mile from Belleview light rail and bus station, per the application
The site was in a Difficult Development Area that expired at the end of 2023; a bond application filed with Denver on 2023-12-11 preserved the 30% basis boost (worth about $4M) until December 2025

money.note: 2024 Round Two; the CHFA letter of intent had estimated $2,405,000.

money.source: Colorado accelerated state housing tax credit
money.note: Application projects $8,100,000 of state credit equity; this is the sponsor's first deal using state credits.

City and County of Denver is the issuer. Council adopted an inducement resolution (24-1446) on 2024-11-04 and passed a bond ordinance (CB25-0165, Series 2025A and 2025B, not to exceed $29M) on 2025-03-03. The application had Zions buying the bonds by private placement and keeping $20,975,000 as the permanent loan; the ordinance names Stifel, Nicolaus as underwriter, U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee and Lument Real Estate Capital as permanent lender.
Subordinate note from the seller, paid off at permanent conversion, per the application.
Paid down to $984,000 at conversion, cash-flow payments, per the application.
The application says no past local, state or federal resources were invested in the project.

parties.name: Stifel, Nicolaus & Company; U.S. Bank Trust Company, N.A.; Lument Real Estate Capital

background.text: Shea submitted conversion plans to Denver in February 2024 and was then under contract to buy the building, next door to its 140-unit Tangent Apartments (built 2019).
Shea closed on the building in April 2025 for $12 million, about $97 per sq ft, per public records cited by BusinessDen. The Real Deal names the seller as Orion Office REIT.

The rezoning was first heard on 2024-06-17 but sent back because three Cherry Hills Village homes within 200 feet had not been notified. Cherry Hills Village's mayor objected (letter dated June 12, 2024) that residents would be stranded without transit, groceries or medical care, and the Greenwood Village mayor also wrote. The re-noticed bill passed 13-0 on 2024-08-12.

The PUD-G 34 covers the whole 12.58-acre parcel, including a second office building to the south that Shea did not buy; existing structures follow S-CC-5 form standards with height and setback flexibility, and new construction would follow S-MX-5.
The project went through Denver's Affordable Housing Review Team (AHRT) process; the planning office recommended approval and recorded four supporting and two opposing comments.
The application cites a 3.6% capture rate, with only three existing non-Section 8 family LIHTC properties in a 38-tract market area, and says no threshold basis waiver was needed.
The application says the project would be infeasible without a 2024 state credit award because the preserved DDA boost would expire in December 2025.
No project-based vouchers or homeless set-aside are described.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award report codes the project as new construction, while CHFA's applicant report and the CHFA letter of intent list it as acquisition/rehab.

The Real Deal reported in November 2024 that Shea bought the property in spring 2024, while BusinessDen reported the purchase closed in April 2025 for $12 million and The Villager described Shea as under contract in March 2024.
The application names Zions as bond purchaser and permanent lender, while the bond ordinance names Lument Real Estate Capital as permanent lender and Stifel, Nicolaus as underwriter.
The Real Deal says Shea secured $6 million of private activity bonds allocated by Denver's housing department, while the application says Denver allocated $17.7 million of bond cap.
